findings.title: Scope fully covers slice-plan entry 129
findings.description: Every item in the slice plan's entry 129 (Part A port to `openai_codex`, bundled-binary-first resolution, optional extra, effort via `ReasoningEffort` closing #171, per-turn usage; Part B exact-install-command error, `sq doctor` row, `sq model list` marker, README; Part C browser + `--device-code` login, `sq auth logout`, email/plan in status, other profiles unchanged, smoke test) maps to an Included item, a decision (D1–D9), or a Success Criterion. Exclusions match the plan (no squadron token store, `login_api_key` out, streaming/approvals unchanged). No assigned scope is dropped.

findings.title: Capability-based dispatch aligns with slice 128 and the architecture's provider invariants
findings.description: D3 and D9 use `runtime_checkable` Protocols with `isinstance` checks instead of profile-name or auth-type string comparisons, directly continuing slice 128's elimination of string dispatch. The provider still registers without the extra so `get_provider` can raise an install hint, keeping the registry complete. Dependency direction is correct: CLI → provider-layer Protocols → `core.usage`; the lazy, function-scoped `openai_codex` imports keep the module graph importable without the optional extra, preserving the "core never depends on provider internals" invariant.

findings.title: Architecture's Authentication Patterns section explicitly reconciled
findings.description: The design addresses the one place it is net-new relative to `100-arch.orchestration-v2.md` ("Squadron does not attempt to unify authentication. Each provider's credential resolution is self-contained.") head-on: `InteractiveLogin` is an optional capability implemented only by the Codex strategy, delegates entirely to the Codex runtime, and squadron stores no credentials (`~/.codex/auth.json` remains the only store). The deferral note ("if a second provider adopts InteractiveLogin, the architecture text should gain a sentence then") is a reasonable boundary call, not a silent deviation.

findings.title: Timeout scope for runtime spawn is internally inconsistent
findings.description: The "Runtime startup cost" paragraph (line 82) asserts that the spawn/`initialize` hang case "is already bounded by `codex.turn_timeout_s`," but the Failure Modes table (line 125) applies that timeout only "around `thread.run`." On the first message, `CodexAgent` performs `AsyncCodex.__aenter__` (subprocess spawn + `initialize`) and `thread_start` before `thread.run`; if the timeout truly wraps only `thread.run`, a hang during spawn or `thread_start` is unbounded, contradicting line 82. The same gap appears on the login path: D7 documents `codex.login_timeout_s` as bounding `handle.wait()` only, while `login.login()` first constructs `AsyncCodex(config)` and calls `login_chatgpt()`/`login_chatgpt_device_code()` (Data Flow, line 84) — a hang in that spawn is not covered by the documented scope, unlike `sq auth status`, where `account_timeout_s` explicitly covers "runtime start + account()." The design should state exactly what each timeout wraps (e.g., turn timeout wraps `__aenter__` + `thread_start` + `thread.run` on first use; login timeout wraps the whole `login.login()` call).

findings.title: Logout I/O path has no enumerated failure modes or timeout
findings.description: `sq auth logout` is a new I/O path — `login.py` performs "async login/logout/account flows over AsyncCodex" and Interfaces Required lists `AsyncCodex.logout()` — yet the Failure Modes table and the Patterns and Conventions list (which names login timeout, login `success=False`, and `account()` failure) contain no row for logout. There is also no timeout covering it: D7 defines `turn`, `login`, and `account` keys but nothing for logout, even though logout spawns the runtime. A hung runtime start or an SDK error during `logout()` has no stated handling strategy (raise vs. warn-and-delete-file vs. report). Add a row (e.g., reuse `codex.account_timeout_s` or the login key, state the exit behavior and what `sq auth status` shows afterward) and a matching test alongside the existing logout test in Technical Requirements.

findings.title: Version upper bound explicitly deferred with a stated default
findings.description: D1 ships a concrete pyproject line (`codex = ["openai-codex>=0.159.3,<1"]`) while Special Considerations leaves "whether to cap" to the PM. Because a default is stated in the design itself, this is not a silent fallback or a blocking TBD — implementation can proceed with `<1` — but the decision should be resolved and recorded in the task file so the final constraint doesn't drift between D1 and the implementation. Also minor: D8 appears after D9 in Technical Decisions (lines 112–114), a numbering slip worth fixing for readability.
